summary: Arizona law does not make working smoke alarms a condition of selling or transferring a home; it requires an approved smoke detector when a home is built, and when a sleeping area is remodeled under a permit.
alarmType: An "approved smoke detector": an electronic device powered by batteries or household current that senses visible or invisible products of combustion and sounds an alarm audible in all sleeping areas, meeting standards set by the Arizona State Fire Marshal under A.R.S. 37-1383. The statute does not require sealed 10-year batteries, hardwiring, interconnection, or photoelectric sensing.
citation: A.R.S. 36-1637 (smoke detectors; residential housing); A.R.S. 36-1636 (definitions); A.R.S. 36-1638 (local ordinances); A.R.S. 36-1639 (exemptions)

Local requirements. A.R.S. 36-1638 expressly preserves city, town and county ordinances that are equal to or stricter than the state rule, and preserves local inspection authority, so an individual Arizona city or county may impose a sale-time or inspection requirement. No local ordinances were checked.
